headline: Protesters storm Microsoft AI data center construction site in Amsterdam
summary: About a hundred activists from the "Stop Dirty Data Centers" coalition broke into a Microsoft data center construction site in Amsterdam, planning broader actions across Europe.
details: A Microsoft data center under construction in Amsterdam, Netherlands, was overrun by approximately a hundred protesters. Some carried placards stating, "Screw your data center," highlighting strong opposition to the project.

The "Stop Dirty Data Centers" coalition organized the action, part of a larger plan for protests across 16 European countries on November 6 and 7, 2026. Other planned sites include Dublin, Warsaw, and another Microsoft location in Denmark.

Pure Data Centers, owner of the Amsterdam site, urged protesters to leave safely and engage in dialogue. Microsoft acknowledged the strong public sentiment and right to peaceful expression but condemned unlawful actions.
The coalition's website calls for an immediate moratorium on large data centers in Europe, citing "irreparable harms" to people and the planet. They plan actions at 85 locations across Europe.

Concerns include impacts on local communities, housing shortages, rising energy bills, the climate crisis, and the erosion of privacy. They argue that big tech undermines democracies and contributes to a toxic supply chain.

Opposition to data centers is a growing issue, with Americans voting against them in midterm elections. European countries are also taking measures to limit their development, such as Denmark halting grid connection requests and an Italian council imposing a 200% tax.

The coalition clarifies they are not against progress or existing projects, but seek clearer government rules for AI data center development. EU tech chief Henna Virkkunen emphasized the need for AI capacity but also citizen trust regarding energy bills and environmental impact.
